To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
keratin expression in pancreatic acini is regulated by virus-induced injury and that keratins are required for acinar regeneration.
keratins 8 and 18 are important for the survival of the exocrine pancreas during coxsackieviral infection.
keratin 8 and 18 (K8/18) are expressed in the acinar cells and ducts of the pancreas and that K8/18 are required to protect acinar cells from injury in the context of coxsackieviruses.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the molecular mechanisms of coxsackieviral-induced pancreatitis, and how keratin 8 and 18 (k8/18), the main intermediate filament proteins of pancreatic acinar cells, affect the pathogenesis of this disease.
the role of keratins in pancreatitis.
the function of keratins in pancreatic injury induced by coxsackieviral infections.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of keratins in the exocrine pancreas is virus dependent and that it may be either protective or detrimental.

the keratin network provides a protective barrier to virus-induced injury, but also a potential site for virus binding and infection, and that the balance between these two functions may be influenced by the type and amount of keratin present.
the keratin network provides a virus-dependent protective function in coxsackie B4-induced pancreatitis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
coxsackieviruses are a common trigger of pancreatitis, which is a serious condition with high morbidity and mortality rates.
coxsackieviruses (CVs) are capable of inducing pancreatitis in mice.
the keratin network is important to maintain the structural integrity of the pancreas, especially under conditions that cause stress, such as viral infection or injury.
The main takeaway from our work is that
keratins protect the pancreas from injury, and that the keratins that do so are different in the adult and neonate.
coxsackieviruses (CoxV) induce pancreatitis in mice that is associated with the expression of keratin 8 and 18 (k8, k18) in acinar cells.
keratin 8 and 18 are important for the integrity of pancreatic ductal epithelial cells.
